 :J U D G M E N T:
This is a claim petition U/Sec.166 of MV Act claiming compensation of Rs.86,00,000/- with interest for the injuries suffered by the petitioner in the Motor Vehicle Accident occurred on 01.10.2019.
2.

The averments of the petition in brief is as follows:
On 01.10.2019 at about 10.10 p.m. after finishing his work the petitioner was returning to home on his motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-04-JK-4887 from Yeshwanthpura to Rajajinagar.

When the petitioner was proceeding in front of Metro cash and carry, the driver of Autorickshaw bearing Reg.No.KA-01-AC-0633 came behind the petitioner in a rash or negligent manner, endangering to human life and suddenly hit the petitioner's bike.
Due to impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately, the driver of Autorickshaw was shifted the petitioner to City Hospital at Rajajinagar, Bangalore.

The petitioner has sustained swelling and tenderness over right clavicle, abrasion over right elbow measuring 3cm., X 2 cm., abrasion over back middle third of right forearm measuring 4 cm., X 3 cm., abrasion over back of right hand measuring 2 cm., X 2 cm., abrasion over left thenar eminence measuring about 3 cm., X 2 cm., abrasion over plantar aspect of right foot measuring about 2 cm., X 1 cm., and fracture mid shaft of right clavicle.
The petitioner has spent a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- towards treatment, medicine, transportation and other miscellaneous expenses and he need amount towards future medical expenses.

The petitioner was aged about 23 years at the time of accident and he was working as a Technical Service Man in fixing and installation of pre-fabricated aluminium mesh windows and doors at UniTech Systems and he was earning a sum of Rs.26,000/- per month.
Due to injuries sustained by the petitioner, he was unable to carryout work and he has been incapacitated and unemployed.
The petitioner is the only earning member in his family.
Due to accidental injuries sustained by him, his family lost his source of income.

The Yeshwanthpura Traffic police have registered the case in crime No.105/2019 against the driver of Autorickshaw bearing Reg.No.KA-01-AC-0633 for the offence punishable under Sec.279, 337 of I.P.C and Sec.134(B), 187 of IMV Act.
Hence, the 1 st respondent being the Insurer and the 2nd respondent being the RC Owner of offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, this petition.
3. After service of notice, 1st Respondent-Insurance company and 2nd respondent- R.C. owner of offending vehicle appeared through their counsels and the 1 st respondent filed written statement.

It Durgaprasad .T.R vs Shri Ram Gen Ins Co Ltd on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139335353/
2 is relevant to note that, the 2nd respondent has not filed written statement.

sentences.text:
4. The written statement averments of the 1st respondent are hereunder:
While admitting the issuance of insurance policy with respect to Autorickshaw bearing Reg.No.KA-01-AC-0633, this respondent restricted its liability subject to the terms and conditions of the policy.

Inter-alia contended that, the driver of offending vehicle has no valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident and the said vehicle was used in public place without having a valid permit and fitness certificate.
This is clear violation of policy conditions by the owner of offending vehicle.

The 2 nd respondent has violated the mandatory provisions of Sec.134 (C) of M.V. Act by not furnishing the vehicle documents and the concerned police have not complied mandatory provisions under Sec.158(6) of M.V. Act.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive.

The 1st respondent contended that, the vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-01-AC-0633 was not at all involved in the accident and it was intentionally implicated in collusion with the driver, owner and other authorities to get the compensation.
The petitioner was riding the bike in a rash or negligent manner without wearing helmet and he is the main architect for the cause of accident.
Hence, prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of the above pleadings, the predecessor in the office has framed the following :ISSUES:
1.
Whether the petitioner proves that he sustained injuries on account of rash and negligent driving of Autorickshaw bearing Reg.No.KA-01-AC-0633 by its driver as contended in the petition?
2. Whether the petitioner proves that, he is entitled for the compensation?

If so, to what extent and from whom?
3. What order or award?
6. In order to prove the case, the petitioner examined himself as P.W.1 and marked Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.12.
Further, he examined Dr. Avinash Parthasarathy as P.W.2 and marked three documents as Ex.P.13 to Ex.P.15.
P.W.1 and P.W.2 were cross-examined from the side of 1st respondent.
The 1st respondent has not adduced evidence.
7. Heard the arguments from both side.
Perused the records placed before the Tribunal.

8. The findings of this Tribunal to the above referred Issues are as under:-
Issue No.1 :- In the Affirmative.

sentences.text: Issue No.3 :- As per the final order, for the following:

:REASONS:
9. ISSUE No.1:-
In order to prove this issue, the petitioner has examined himself as P.W.1 by way of filing affidavit in support of his oral examination-in-chief.
Hence, this Tribunal need not to recapitulate the same once again at this juncture.
P.W.1 has relied on Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.8.

Accordingly,
Ex.P.1 is the true copy of charge sheet.
Ex . P.2
is the true copy of FIR.
Ex . P.3
is the true copy of complaint.
Ex . P.4
is the true copy of Spot mahazar.
Ex. P.4(a) is the spot sketch.
Ex. P.5
is the true copy of notice issued under Sec.133 of I.M.V. Act.
Ex . P.6
is the true copy of reply notice.
Ex. P.7
is the true copy of M.V.A. report.
Ex.P.8 is the true copy of wound certificate.

10. At this juncture it is worth to refer the decision reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530 between Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has observed that, "it is necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.

entities.text: Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The claimants are merely required to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied".
11. According to the petitioner, he has sustained injuries in the road accident.

According to the respondent No.1, at the time of accident, petitioner was not wearing helmet and the accident was occurred due to negligent riding of the petitioner and not due to negligent act of the driver of offending vehicle.
In order to substantiate the defence, respondent No.1 has not placed positive evidence.
Likewise, 1st respondent neither examined the driver of offending vehicle nor ocular witnesses to the incident to establish its defence.
12. Further, to prove the alleged negligence on the part of petitioner, the Insurance Company has cross- examined the petitioner/P.W.1 in detail.
Nothing has been elicited from mouth of P.W.1 to establish that the accident was took place only on the negligence of petitioner.
At the cost of repetition, to substantiate its contention, Insurance company has not placed positive evidence.
13. In the instant case, the petitioner has produced police documents.
As per Ex.P.3, complaint was lodged before Yeshwanthapura Police Station.
Thereafter, as per Ex.P.2, FIR was lodged against the driver of Autorickshaw bearing Reg.No.KA-01-AC-0633.

On careful perusal of Ex.P.2, Ex.P.3 and Ex.P.1, it appears to this Tribunal that, on the basis of complaint, the police have registered the case against the driver of Autorickshaw bearing Reg.No.KA- 01-AC-0633 and Investigating officer has submitted the Charge sheet as per Ex.P.1 after completing investigation.

A careful perusal of Ex.P.8,
it clearly goes to show that, the injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.

Further, on perusal of Ex.P.1 i.e., final report, it reveals that, the driver of offending vehicle i.e.,
Autorickshaw bearing Reg.No.KA-01-AC-0633 has been arrayed as an accused.

14. At the cost of repetition, the contents of complaint and charge sheet clearly reveals that, when the petitioner was riding the Motor Cycle bearing Reg.No.KA- 04-JK-4887, the driver of Durgaprasad .T.R vs Shri Ram Gen Ins Co Ltd on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139335353/

sentences.text: Autorickshaw
bearing
Reg.No.KA-01-AC-0633 came in a rash or negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner's motor cycle.
The evidence placed on record is clearly reveals that driver of the offending vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-01-AC-0633 has caused the accident.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
15. ISSUE No.2:- This issue is with respect to entitlement of relief.
Already this Tribunal has observed that, accident was occurred due to rash or negligent driving of the Autorickshaw bearing Reg.No.KA-01-AC- 0633.

The 1st respondent is the Insurer and the 2nd respondent is the R.C.
owner of the offending vehicle.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation.
Before going to discuss other aspects, it is appropriate to discuss the age and income of the petitioner.
According to the petitioner, he was aged 23 years as on the date of accident.
In order to substantiate the same, the petitioner has produced Ex.P.12 the notarized copy of his Driving Lincence.
On perusal of this document it appears to this Tribunal that, the date of birth of petitioner is mentioned as 12.09.1995.
The accident was occurred on 01-10-2019.
Hence, as on the date of accident the age of the petitioner was 24 years.
Accordingly the age of the petitioner is considered as 24 years.
17. Income:-

According to the petitioner, he was working as a Technician and earning Rs.26,000/-
per month.
Per- contra, the 1st Respondent has denied the income of petitioner.
To substantiate the income of petitioner, he has produced Ex.P.9, the salary certificate issued by the Unitech Systems.
However, he has not examined the employer to substantiate the contents of Ex.P.9.
Hence, Ex.P.9 will not come to the aid of petitioner to prove his salary.

Therefore, at this juncture, it is worth to rely on the decision of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka decided in M.F.A. No.101144 of 2020 (MV-I) on 05.07.2023, between Ananda Vs. Arun and Another, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka at Para 9 (b) as hereunder:
" In the absence of any cogent material on record, it is for the Courts and Tribunals to assess the income notionally.
The notional income fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority for the accident of the year 2017 is Rs.10,250/-.

In the absence of any material produced by the claimant to prove his income, it is appropriate to assess the notional income of the injured claimant at Rs.10,250/- per month, and the same is assessed as the monthly income of the injured claimant".

18. In the absence of reliable document and supportive evidence, the notional income of the petitioner is to be considered by relying on the Judgment of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka referred to above.
As per the notional income fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority for the accident in the year 2019 is Rs.14,000/- per month.
It is pertinent to note that, the accident took place on 01-10-2019.

Hence, the notional income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.14,000./-
per month.

19. Loss of Future Income due to disability:-

In the instant case, the petitioner has averred that, he has sustained swelling and tenderness over right clavicle, abrasion over right elbow, abrasion over back middle 3 rd of right forearm, abrasion over back of right hand, abrasion over left thenar eminence, abrasion over planter aspect of right foot.
P.W.1 has stated the same in his affidavit filed in support of his oral examination in chief.
He has produced wound certificate which is marked as Ex.P.8.
On perusal of Ex.P.8-Wound certificate it reveals that, the petitioner has sustained aforesaid injuries.

It is relevant to mention that, respondent No.1 has disputed the injuries caused to P.W.1.
20.
In order to prove the physical disability/injuries, the petitioner has examined medical witness namely Dr. Avanish Parthasarathi as P.W.2.
This witness has filed the affidavit in lieu of evidence and stated that the petitioner has sustained fracture right clavicle and he was treated conservatively.
Further deposed that, the petitioner was admitted on 01.10.2019 and discharged on 02.10.2019.
Further deposed that, on 08.01.2024 he examined the petitioner.
Finally he has assessed the permanent physical impairment of petitioner as 33% and 11% to the whole body.
He was cross-examined from the side of 1st respondent at length.

During the course of cross-examination,
he has admitted that, he was not the treated doctor.
He has admitted that, the petitioner was treated conservatively.
He also deposed that, he only assessed physical disability of petitioner.
He denied the suggestion that, clavicle bone is an ornamental bone.
Further, he has denied that, there is no disability to the petitioner since clavicle bone is an ornamental bone.

P.W.2 has produced four documents, where are marked as Ex.P.13 to Ex.P.15.
21.
In the instant case, the petitioner has not produced the discharge summary.
On perusal of the wound certificate of petitioner and evidence of medical witness clearly reveals that, petitioner has sustained injuries and suffered physical disability.
However, the petitioner has taken conservative treatment.
Learned counsel for the respondent No.1 relied on two decisions of our Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka.

The said decisions are worth to reproduce here itself: M.F.A.No.1602/2016,
between Jayanth Kumar B., Vs. M.J. Mahesha and Another and M.F.A.No.10220/2010, between Nataraju Vs. H.S. Sidda Rajaiah and Another.

sentences.text: "The records clearly disclose that due to the actionable negligence on the part of the rider of the scooter, the claimant fell down and sustained fracture of clavicle bone on 19.03.2009.
He has taken treatment in the District Hospital, Mandya.
He was treated conservatively and he has not undergone any surgery, he has submitted the medical bill for Rs.6,000/-.
The doctor who issued the disability certificate is not the treated doctor.
For the fracture of clavicle bone, the doctor has assessed the disability to an extent of 20% which is contrary to law.
The clavicle bone is only an ornamental bone and the said fracture does not lead to any disability.
In the instant case, the disability assessed by the doctor is contrary to law.

The Tribunal taking into Durgaprasad .T.R vs Shri Ram Gen Ins Co Ltd on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139335353/
6 consideration the injuries sustained and suffering undergone awarded just and fair compensation.

sentences.text: The appellant has not made out a case to interfere with the said judgment and award.

Accordingly the appeal is dismissed".
22.
In the instant case also, P.W.2 in his affidavit has clearly stated that, the petitioner has sustained fracture of right clavicle bone and he was treated conservatively.
Hence, the above referred decision is aptly applicable to the case on hand.
Per-contra the decision relied by the petitioner is rendered in a factually distinguishable case.
Hence, the decision relied by the petitioner will not come to the aid of petitioner.
Therefore, this Tribunal considered that, the petitioner is not entitled for any compensation under the head loss of Future Income due to disabiltiy.
23. Medical Expenses:-
In the instant case, the petitioner has stated that, he has incurred Rs.1,00,000/- towards medical expenses, transportation and other incidental expenses.
In order to substantiate the incurring of medical expenses, the petitioner has produced 13 medical bills marked as Ex.P.10 for Rs.13,984.19.
This Tribunal has carefully perused Ex.P.10, the medical bills coupled with Trip Sheet.
To substantiate the expenses incurred towards travelling, he has not examined the author of Trip sheet.
Hence, the petitioner is not entitled for the amount mentioned in Trip Sheet.
After careful perusal of the medical bills, this Tribunal is of the opinion that, petitioner is entitled for Rs.7,906/- towards medical expenses.
24. Pain and suffering:-
According to the petitioner, immediately after the accident, he was shifted to City Hospital, Rajajinagar, Bengaluru, wherein he was treated for injuries.
Already this Tribunal has observed that, the petitioner has taken conservative treatment.
On perusal of Ex.P.13, the Outpatient Record reveals that, on 08.01.2024, P.W.2 has examined the petitioner and the fracture of right clavicle is malunited.
As such, the petitioner has suffered certain pain and inconvenience.
Considering all these aspects, the Tribunal grants compensation of Rs.30,000/- under the head of Pain and Sufferings.
25. Loss of income during the laidup period:- The petitioner has not produced discharge summary.
The petitioner has not produced document to show that, how many days he has taken bed rest.
The petitioner has sustained fracture of right clavicle bone.
Naturally it shows that, he might have taken atleast one month rest because of the injury.
He has averred that, he was a Technicial by profession and earning Rs.26,000/- per month.
But he has not produced documents to substantiate the same.
Hence, this Tribunal has already assessed the income of petitioner as Rs.14,000/- per month.
Hence, one month is to be considered as loss of income during laidup period.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.14,000/- as compensation under the head of loss of income during laid up period.
26. Food, Nourishment and Atttendant charges:-
In so for as food, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges are concerned, the Petitioner has taken conservative treatment.
The Petitioner has not produced any documents to show that, he has taken treatment as an inpatient.

Hence, looking to the injuries sustained and the period of treatment taken by the petitioner, he is entitled for compensation of Rs.2,000/- under the head of Food,

27. Loss of future amenities and happiness:- The Petitioner was aged about 24 years at the time of accident.
The disability and physical deformity with which the petitioner has to live the rest of his life.
Therefore, he might have suffered pain, discomforts in life and loss of amenities.
By considering the age, nature of injuries, percentage of disabiltiy, Rs.20,000/- is awarded under this head.

28. Thus, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
 Heads Amount  1.Towards loss of Future income.
- Nil -  2. Towards Medical Expenses.
3. Towards Pain & Suffering.

4. Loss of income during the  Rs. 14,000/-
 laidup period  5. Food, Nourishment and Rs. 2,000/-

Atttendant charges:
 6. Loss of future amenities and Rs. 20,000/-
 happiness.

Total. Rs.73,906/-
Hence, petitioner is entitled for just and reasonable amount of Rs.73,906/-
29.
Regarding liability and interest.
Driving License:-
According to respondsent No.1, the driver of offending vehicle has no valid driving licence to drive the vehicle.
However, respondent No.1 has not adduced any evidence.
Charge sheet submitted by IO does not reveals that driver of offending vehicle was driving the vehicle without valid and effective DL as on the date of accident.
On perusal of Ex.P.6, it reveals that, the R.C. owner cum driver of offending vehicle has clearly mentioned his driving licence number and its validity as on the date of accident.
Therefore, it appears to this Tribunal that, the Driver of the offending vehicle was holding valid D.L. to drive the offending vehicle at the time of accident.
Insurance Policy and liability:- Respondent No.1- the insurance company has admitted the issuance of insurance policy with respect to offending vehicle.
Hence, it is held that, insurance coverage of the vehicle was in force at the time of accident.
Hence, the respondent No.1 shall pay compensation amount to the petitioners.

30. In view of the decision reported in MFA NO:

31. ISSUE No.3:- In view of discussions made above, I proceed to pass the following.

:ORDER:
Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner U/Sec.166 of M.V. Act is partly allowed with costs of the petition.
Petitioner is awarded just and reasonable compensation of Rs.73,906/- (Rupees Seventy Three Thousand Nine Hundred and Six only) with interest at the rate of 6%
p.a., from the date of petition to till the date of depositing of the compensation amount in the Tribunal.
Respondent No.1 shall deposit the compensation in the Tribunal within 2 months from the date of this judgment.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw Award Accordingly.

:APPORTIONMENT:
Scheme of investment is dispensed with as amount awarded is too meager.

This is a claim petition U/Sec.166 of MV Act claiming compensation of Rs.86,00,000/- with interest for the injuries suffered by the petitioner in the Motor Vehicle Accident occurred on 01.10.2019.

opennyai_summary.facts:
The Yeshwanthpura Traffic police have registered the case in crime No.105/2019 against the driver of Autorickshaw bearing Reg.No.KA-01-AC-0633 for the offence punishable under Sec.279, 337 of I.P.C and Sec.134(B), 187 of IMV Act.
Hence, the 1 st respondent being the Insurer and the 2nd respondent being the RC Owner of offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Inter-alia contended that, the driver of offending vehicle has no valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident and the said vehicle was used in public place without having a valid permit and fitness certificate.
This is clear violation of policy conditions by the owner of offending vehicle.
The 2 nd respondent has violated the mandatory provisions of Sec.134 (C) of M.V. Act by not furnishing the vehicle documents and the concerned police have not complied mandatory provisions under Sec.158(6) of M.V. Act.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive.
The 1st respondent contended that, the vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-01-AC-0633 was not at all involved in the accident and it was intentionally implicated in collusion with the driver, owner and other authorities to get the compensation.
opennyai_summary.issue:
Whether the petitioner proves that he sustained injuries on account of rash and negligent driving of Autorickshaw bearing Reg.No.KA-01-AC-0633 by its driver as contended in the petition?
2. Whether the petitioner proves that, he is entitled for the compensation?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
10. At this juncture it is worth to refer the decision reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530 between Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has observed that, "it is necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.
Likewise, 1st respondent neither examined the driver of offending vehicle nor ocular witnesses to the incident to establish its defence.
Nothing has been elicited from mouth of P.W.1 to establish that the accident was took place only on the negligence of petitioner.
At the cost of repetition, to substantiate its contention, Insurance company has not placed positive evidence.
Hence, Ex.P.9 will not come to the aid of petitioner to prove his salary.
In the absence of any material produced by the claimant to prove his income, it is appropriate to assess the notional income of the injured claimant at Rs.10,250/- per month, and the same is assessed as the monthly income of the injured claimant".
On perusal of the wound certificate of petitioner and evidence of medical witness clearly reveals that, petitioner has sustained injuries and suffered physical disability.
The Tribunal taking into Durgaprasad .T.R vs Shri Ram Gen Ins Co Ltd on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139335353/
6 consideration the injuries sustained and suffering undergone awarded just and fair compensation.
This Tribunal has carefully perused Ex.P.10, the medical bills coupled with Trip Sheet.
To substantiate the expenses incurred towards travelling, he has not examined the author of Trip sheet.
Hence, the petitioner is not entitled for the amount mentioned in Trip Sheet.
As such, the petitioner has suffered certain pain and inconvenience.
25. Loss of income during the laidup period:- The petitioner has not produced discharge summary.
The petitioner has sustained fracture of right clavicle bone.
But he has not produced documents to substantiate the same.
Hence, this Tribunal has already assessed the income of petitioner as Rs.14,000/- per month.

:ORDER:
Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner U/Sec.166 of M.V. Act is partly allowed with costs of the petition.
Petitioner is awarded just and reasonable compensation of Rs.73,906/- (Rupees Seventy Three Thousand Nine Hundred and Six only) with interest at the rate of 6%
p.a., from the date of petition to till the date of depositing of the compensation amount in the Tribunal.

Draw Award Accordingly.

Scheme of investment is dispensed with as amount awarded is too meager.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
In the instant case also, P.W.2 in his affidavit has clearly stated that, the petitioner has sustained fracture of right clavicle bone and he was treated conservatively.
In the instant case, the petitioner has stated that, he has incurred Rs.1,00,000/- towards medical expenses, transportation and other incidental expenses.
In order to substantiate the incurring of medical expenses, the petitioner has produced 13 medical bills marked as Ex.P.10 for Rs.13,984.19.
Hence, one month is to be considered as loss of income during laidup period.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.14,000/- as compensation under the head of loss of income during laid up period.
26. Food, Nourishment and Atttendant charges:-
In so for as food, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges are concerned, the Petitioner has taken conservative treatment.
The Petitioner has not produced any documents to show that, he has taken treatment as an inpatient.
Hence, looking to the injuries sustained and the period of treatment taken by the petitioner, he is entitled for compensation of Rs.2,000/- under the head of Food,
